rules.cwe_name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
rules.description: Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
rules.description: Using a named argument whose name does not correspond to a parameter of the __init__ method of the class being instantiated, will result in a TypeError at runtime.

rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.

rules.cwe_name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
rules.description: A regular expression that requires exponential time to match certain inputs can be a performance bottleneck, and may be vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
rules.description: Using user-controlled data to create a template can lead to remote code execution or cross site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
rules.description: Extracting files from a potentially malicious tarball using `shutil.unpack_archive()` without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can cause files outside the destination directory to be overwritten. rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
rules.description: Building a NoSQL query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious NoSQL code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
rules.description: The built-in function 'input' is used which, in Python 2, can allow arbitrary code to be run.

rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
rules.description: Cookies without the `HttpOnly` attribute set can be accessed by JS scripts, making them more vulnerable to XSS attacks.
